question.name: CSEC Bio Jan 2024 Q1b(i)(ii) — Diabetes: Dietary Changes and Consequences
question.text:
Roy has been diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes. He is advised to make dietary changes.

(i) Suggest TWO dietary changes Roy should make: (2 marks)

Change 1: [[1]]

Change 2: [[2]]

(ii) State ONE consequence for Roy if he does NOT follow each dietary change: (2 marks)

Consequence of not following Change 1: [[3]]

Consequence of not following Change 2: [[4]]
question.general_feedback:
Dietary management of Type 2 diabetes:

Recommended changes:

  • Reduce carbohydrate intake — carbohydrates are broken down to glucose; excess glucose raises blood sugar
  • Avoid/reduce sugar and sugary foods — sugar directly raises blood glucose levels
  • Increase dietary fibre — fibre slows glucose absorption, preventing blood sugar spikes
  • Maintain a healthy weight — obesity worsens insulin resistance

Consequences if changes are NOT followed:

  • Persistently high blood glucose (hyperglycaemia)
  • Damage to blood vessels and nerves — leading to complications such as kidney disease (nephropathy), loss of vision (retinopathy), nerve damage (neuropathy), poor wound healing
  • Risk of diabetic coma (diabetic ketoacidosis in severe cases)

groups.label: Dietary change 1 for managing diabetes
groups.diagnostic_hint: Diabetes management focuses on keeping blood glucose stable. Reducing carbohydrates and avoiding sugary foods directly reduces the glucose load entering the blood.

groups.label: Dietary change 2 for managing diabetes
groups.diagnostic_hint: A second dietary change addresses a different aspect: increasing dietary fibre slows glucose absorption, preventing sharp glucose spikes after meals.

groups.label: Consequence 1 of not managing diabetes diet
groups.diagnostic_hint: Without dietary management, blood glucose stays persistently high — a condition called hyperglycaemia. This is the primary consequence of uncontrolled diabetes.

groups.label: Consequence 2 of not managing diabetes diet
groups.diagnostic_hint: Prolonged hyperglycaemia damages small blood vessels, causing complications in the kidneys (nephropathy), eyes (retinopathy), and nerves (neuropathy).

ddwtos.word_bank_note: 10 tokens for 4 slots. Dietary changes (slots 1-2): any 2 of the 3 correct changes earn full marks. 'Increase fat intake' is wrong — high fat worsens cardiovascular risk in diabetes. 'Avoid protein' is wrong — protein does not raise blood glucose and is not restricted in standard diabetic diet advice. Consequences (slots 3-4): any 2 of the 3 correct consequences earn full marks. 'Hypoglycaemia (low blood glucose)' is the OPPOSITE problem — it results from too much insulin or insufficient eating, not from failing to follow a diabetic diet. 'Vitamin C deficiency' is irrelevant to blood glucose management.
